caveats: Yahoo 5-minute data is not a 4-minute strategy or historical options pricing.
Each symbol is simulated independently with $500; summed profit is NOT portfolio P/L.
Experiment selection is TRAIN-ONLY; holdout is descriptive and not used for choosing.
Repeated daily research can overfit the same holdout; independent future validation is required.
No validated aggregate portfolio drawdown or options transaction costs.

previous_batch_comparison.caveat: Historical same-symbol holdout is a diagnostic comparison, not an independent prospective validation.

adaptive_learning.method: Cumulative historical TRAIN-only expectancy; no holdout-based tuning
adaptive_learning.caution: Repeated stock histories may overlap across batches and reruns. Cumulative evidence is not independent and does not validate a live edge.

last_week_evaluation.description: Last five available trading sessions per stock; independent $500 per-symbol stock simulations, not a shared $500 portfolio

improvement_agent.next_action: Inspect loss reasons; test entry filters, exits, risk/reward and market regimes on identical historical windows.
improvement_agent.warning: Repeated use of the same holdout overfits it; this is a diagnostic, not independent validation.

questions: Which losing trades were caused by countertrend entries, spread/slippage, or market chop?
Would filtering low relative volume or EMA/VWAP misalignment improve OUT-OF-SAMPLE net expectancy?
What happens to trade frequency and profit after realistic options bid/ask and fees?
Does the candidate outperform the unchanged baseline across multiple dates and symbols?
Are the improvements statistically robust, or just overfit to the recent losers?
